veredicto.titulo: Lectura de la postrera 2026 para planificar 2027: frijol en relevo tras maíz (práctica actual), confianza baja
Lectura de la postrera 2026 para planificar 2027: frijol en relevo tras maíz (práctica actual), confianza baja
veredicto.texto: Ninguna opción gana en todos los escenarios. Frijol en relevo tras maíz (práctica actual) es la que mejor aguanta el peor caso: en 6 escenarios su puntaje más bajo es 0,799, frente a 0,791 de sorgo (maicillo) + frijol. Queda primera o empatada en 4 de 6 y, cuando no, como mucho 0,016 puntos detrás.

condiciones.texto: Margen entre las dos mejores: 0,007 (umbral de lectura 0,05, un SUPUESTO).
Sin la regla de 150 mm del frijol, la elección cambia en 24 de 25 años.
Con NASA POWER en lugar de IMERG, la elección cambia en 9 de 25 años.
Prueba de sequías documentadas: el modelo distingue los años de sequía citados.

razones_lectura: Las estrategias quedan a menos de 0,02 puntos entre sí; la primera supera a la segunda por menos de 0,05.
En la validación 2001–2025, elegir siempre la misma estrategia empata o supera a Tempo.

recomendacion.texto: Ninguna opción gana en todos los escenarios. Frijol en relevo tras maíz (práctica actual) es la que mejor aguanta el peor caso: en 6 escenarios su puntaje más bajo es 0,799, frente a 0,791 de sorgo (maicillo) + frijol. Queda primera o empatada en 4 de 6 y, cuando no, como mucho 0,016 puntos detrás.
limites: Las pruebas estrictas fallan: en los años pasados la elección cambia sin la regla de 150 mm del frijol o con otra fuente de lluvia. La confianza no puede ser alta.
En el escenario base ninguna alternativa supera a la práctica actual por 0,05 o más (diferencia 0,016): no hay razón para cambiar.

strategies.label: Current: relay bean after maize
strategies.description: The usual system: beans sown between the maize rows once the primera maize matures. Short cycle, fixes nitrogen, but sensitive to both drought and heavy late rains.
strategies.why: In 8 past years with a long canícula like 2026, this strategy scored 0.81 on average (1 = good harvest, 0 = failure) and failed in 0% of them.
benefits: Fixes nitrogen for the next primera.
Keeps more of the soil covered.
Lower water demand than the alternatives.
gaps: Rainfall is a ~10 km satellite cell (IMERG) or a ~55 km model cell (POWER), not the parcel. IMERG is known to miss part of the rain in mountain terrain.
Crop parameters (cycle, water use) are FAO-56 defaults not yet validated by a local agronomist.
Mixed-plot land shares (0.6 / 0.4) and the bean excess-rain threshold (150 mm at maturity) are assumptions; yields are not modeled.
Soil data is SoilGrids at 250 m unless the technician enters field data.
risks: Beans are hit by both drought at flowering and heavy rain at maturity.
Short ground cover: soil is bare again by December.

strategies.label: Sorghum + bean
strategies.description: Part of the plot goes to drought-tolerant sorghum (grain and forage), the rest to beans. Deep roots and longer ground cover protect sloped soil.
strategies.why: In 8 past years with a long canícula like 2026, this strategy scored 0.93 on average (1 = good harvest, 0 = failure) and failed in 0% of them.
benefits: Fixes nitrogen for the next primera.
Keeps more of the soil covered.
gaps: Rainfall is a ~10 km satellite cell (IMERG) or a ~55 km model cell (POWER), not the parcel. IMERG is known to miss part of the rain in mountain terrain.
Crop parameters (cycle, water use) are FAO-56 defaults not yet validated by a local agronomist.
Mixed-plot land shares (0.6 / 0.4) and the bean excess-rain threshold (150 mm at maturity) are assumptions; yields are not modeled.
Soil data is SoilGrids at 250 m unless the technician enters field data.
risks: Sorghum is less valued as human food than maize or beans.
Longer cycle: sorghum harvest falls into the dry season (December-January).
Seed of local sorghum (maicillo) varieties must be confirmed.

strategies.label: Second maize
strategies.description: A second maize crop instead of beans, to rebuild the grain reserve after a lost primera. Highest water demand of the three and no nitrogen return.
strategies.why: In 8 past years with a long canícula like 2026, this strategy scored 1.0 on average (1 = good harvest, 0 = failure) and failed in 0% of them.
gaps: Rainfall is a ~10 km satellite cell (IMERG) or a ~55 km model cell (POWER), not the parcel. IMERG is known to miss part of the rain in mountain terrain.
Crop parameters (cycle, water use) are FAO-56 defaults not yet validated by a local agronomist.
Mixed-plot land shares (0.6 / 0.4) and the bean excess-rain threshold (150 mm at maturity) are assumptions; yields are not modeled.
Soil data is SoilGrids at 250 m unless the technician enters field data.
risks: Highest water demand; late planting pushes grain filling into the dry season.
No nitrogen returned to the soil; maize after maize depletes it.
Skipping the bean crop removes the household's main protein and cash crop.

sensitivity.method: leave-one-out hindcast re-run per variant; pick changes vs the baseline run

primera_check.rank_method: max (ties take the highest rank; 1 = driest)

hindcast.method: leave-one-out by canicula tercile; hit/fallo only for cited drought years (D6), primera maize WRSI in the worst third (ties ranked max); no_evaluable when CHECK 1 is not discriminative

years.source: FAO, 29 Jun 2016, ReliefWeb GLIDE DR-2014-000132-HND (https://reliefweb.int/disaster/dr-2014-000132-hnd): loss of staple grain crops in El Salvador since mid-2014.
ReliefWeb GLIDE DR-2018-000106-SLV (https://reliefweb.int/disaster/dr-2018-000106-slv): over 90,000 metric tons of corn lost, red alert.
